faqs.a: APY stands for annual percentage yield. It is the real yearly return on savings after compounding, while the nominal rate is the stated rate before compounding. The same 5% nominal rate gives a higher APY when compounded more often.

Use APY to compare savings and deposit accounts, because it reflects what you actually earn. Use APR to compare borrowing costs, because it reflects what you actually pay. They answer opposite questions.
faqs.q: Should I compare APY or APR?

faqs.a: More frequent compounding always raises APY a little. Daily compounding on a 5% nominal rate gives 5.1267% APY versus 5.1162% for monthly, a difference of about one dollar per year on a 10,000 balance.
Yes. In many countries banks must advertise APY so savers can compare accounts fairly. It is sometimes called the effective annual rate or AER.
faqs.q: Is APY the rate banks advertise?

faqs.a: They can differ when fees eat into returns or when the rate changes during the year. This calculator shows the pure compounding effect; read the account terms for fees and tiered rates.
faqs.q: Can APY differ from my actual return?

faqs.a: APY = (1 + nominal / m)^m - 1, where m is the number of compounding periods per year. As m grows very large it approaches continuous compounding, e^nominal - 1.

apy-calculator.formula:
APY = (1 + nominal_rate / m)^m - 1
m = compounding periods per year (1, 2, 4, 12, 52, 365)
year_end_value = deposit x (1 + APY)
howTo: Enter the nominal (advertised) annual interest rate.
Choose how often interest is compounded.
Read the true APY, the rate earned each period and the year-end value of a 1,000 deposit.
Try different frequencies to see how compounding changes the return.
keyFacts: APY, the annual percentage yield, is the effective yearly return after compounding is included.
The same nominal rate produces a higher APY when interest compounds more frequently.
A 5% nominal rate compounded monthly is 5.116% APY; compounded daily it is 5.127% APY.
APY is the standard number for comparing savings accounts, CDs and money-market accounts.
The difference between APY and the nominal rate is small at low rates but grows as rates rise.

apy-calculator.quickAnswer: APY is the real yearly return after compounding. A 5% nominal rate compounded monthly equals 5.116% APY, so 10,000 grows to 10,511.62 in one year — slightly more than the nominal rate suggests.
apy-calculator.tagline: Turn any nominal rate into its true yearly yield.
apy-calculator.workedExample:
Nominal rate 5%, compounded monthly (m = 12).

APY = (1 + 0.05/12)^12 - 1 = 1.00416667^12 - 1 = 1.0511619 - 1 = 5.116%.

Rate per period = 5 / 12 = 0.4167%. A 10,000 deposit grows to 10,000 x 1.0511619 = $10,511.62 in one year. Compounded daily instead, APY = (1 + 0.05/365)^365 - 1 = 5.127%.
